preface.p: An Act to amend the Customs Act 1901, and for related purposes
An Act to amend the Customs Act 1901, and for related purposes

content.p: This Act may be cited as the Customs Amendment Act 2015.
This Act commences on the day after this Act receives the Royal Assent.

Each Act that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

section.heading: Goods on ships and aircraft subject to Customs control

content.p: All goods on board any ship or aircraft from a place outside Australia are subject to the control of the Customs while the ship or aircraft:
is within the limits of any port or airport in Australia; or
is at a place to which the ship or aircraft has been brought because of stress of weather or other reasonable cause as mentioned in subsection 58(1); or
is at a place that is the subject of a permission under subsection 58(2).

section.heading: General powers of examination of goods loaded onto or unloaded from ships or aircraft

content.p: This section applies in relation to the following:
a ship or aircraft in respect of a voyage or flight to a place in Australia from a place outside Australia;
a ship or aircraft in respect of a voyage or flight to a place outside Australia from a place in Australia.
Goods to be loaded onto the ship or aircraft
If:
an officer has reason to believe that goods are to be loaded onto the ship or aircraft at an examinable place; and
the goods are to be unloaded at another examinable place on the same voyage or flight;
then:
any officer may, subject to subsections (5) and (6), examine the goods while the goods are at the examinable place mentioned in paragraph (a); and
the goods are subject to the control of the Customs while the goods are being so examined.
Goods unloaded from the ship or aircraft
If:
goods are loaded onto the ship or aircraft at an examinable place; and
the goods are unloaded from the ship or aircraft at another examinable place on the same voyage or flight;
then:
any officer may, subject to subsections (5) and (6), examine the goods while the goods are at the examinable place mentioned in paragraph (b); and
the goods are subject to the control of the Customs while the goods are being so examined.
Rules relating to examination of goods
The expense of an examination referred to in subsection (2) or (3), including the cost of removal to the place of examination, is to be borne by the owner of the goods.

In the exercise of the power to examine goods, an officer may do, or arrange for another officer or other person having the necessary experience to do, whatever is reasonably necessary to permit the examination of the goods.
Without limiting subsection (5), examples of what may be done in the examination of goods include the following:
opening any package in which goods are or may be contained;
using a device, such as an X-ray machine or ion scanning equipment, on the goods;
testing or analysing the goods;
measuring or counting the goods;
if the goods are a document—reading the document either directly or with the use of an electronic device;
using dogs to assist in examining the goods.
No limit on other provisions
This section does not:
limit the application of any other provision of this Act that provides for goods to be subject to the control of the Customs; and
limit the application of any other provision of this Act that provides for the examination of goods.
Definition
In this section:
examinable place means the following:
a port or airport in Australia (whether the first port or airport or any subsequent port or airport on the same voyage or flight);
a place to which a ship or aircraft has been brought because of stress of weather or other reasonable cause as mentioned in subsection 58(1);
a place that is the subject of a permission under subsection 58(2).
